clue.text: Punished mainly by the captain

parts.note: 'mainly' looks like 'for the most part' but means 'by way of the main', the sea: an old naval punishment dragging a sailor under the ship's bottom

explanation.surface: A captain who doles out most of the discipline on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' reads as 'chiefly', but it is the main, the open sea: the sailor is dragged under the vessel from side to side.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragging a sailor beneath the hull was a historical shipboard punishment ordered by a captain.

clue.text: It's almost a sin in Ireland!

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to err is to sin
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is nearly sinful in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sin' gives ERR, cut short by 'almost' to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland.

clue.text: Compares rights around kampuchea

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the word for rights goes round the letter for Kampuchea

parts.note: liens are legal rights to hold property against a debt
K was the international vehicle code for Kampuchea, now Cambodia

explanation.surface: Weighing up rights in Cambodia.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to draw a comparison.

clue.text: A surprise may so daunt

indicators.note: may suggests possibility, so the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A shock that could intimidate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' signals that SO DAUNT could be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to shock or amaze them.

clue.text: Look about and gain knowledge

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone looks around and learns something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge passed down within a group.

clue.text: Ancient city some French first lay waste

indicators.note: first places the French word at the front, before the city

parts.note: des is French for some
Troy was the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: French forces first lay waste to an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to ruin completely.

clue.text: A degree of excitement fellow will always get on sports field

parts.note: ever means always
a pitch is a playing field

explanation.surface: A chap will always turn up at the sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is an intense level of agitation or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Degrees to which darts go in a different direction

indicators.note: going in a different direction suggests the letters are sent elsewhere into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of how far darts veer off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different direction' rearranges DARTS GO IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradations are steps or stages on a scale, a series of degrees.

clue.text: Told to peel the fruit

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the word for peel is heard rather than written

parts.note: to peel fruit is to pare it

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to peel a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A juicy orchard fruit narrower at the stalk end, grown on a tree related to the apple.

clue.text: Boots loose women — then gets going!

parts.note: to boot something is to kick it, so boots means kicks
tarts is a slang term for promiscuous women

explanation.surface: A bouncer throws out some disreputable women and then sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a stalled engine or project with a sudden push is to get it going.

clue.text: Tread hard, difficult thin line

indicators.note: difficult here signals that the letters are worked awkwardly into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Walking heavily along a tricky narrow path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges TREAD plus H (hard) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single strand of cotton or silk is a very fine line of fibre.

clue.text: Gift is here, having been despatched earlier

definitions.meaning: here means in attendance, not absent

explanation.surface: A gift has arrived, having been posted ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: a gift, in attendance, and, split as PRE-SENT, already sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a present, someone here is present, and something sent ahead is pre-sent.

clue.text: He has more than one rib

definitions.text: He has more than one rib

parts.words: He has more than one rib
parts.note: a rib is a jocular term for a wife, after Eve being made from Adam's rib, so this man has several spouses

explanation.surface: A man has an extra bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' seems anatomical, but it is slang for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A man with several wives practises plural marriage.

clue.text: In peril of death — getting furious

parts.note: death is one's end
angered means made furious

explanation.surface: Someone in mortal danger is growing furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A species or person under threat is at risk, in danger.

clue.text: Signs of grief after one splits

definitions.meaning: drops shed from the eyes when crying

explanation.surface: Crying after someone splits up.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying sheds drops from the eyes; ripping cloth also rends it.

clue.text: Tropical locality that's potentially explosive

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a place where the weather is very warm
a trouble area liable to erupt into violence

explanation.surface: A warm-climate region that may be about to erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a sweltering place; figuratively a dangerous flashpoint of conflict.

clue.text: Barren patch for an old prime minister?

definitions.meaning: an open uncultivated stretch of land

explanation.surface: Some infertile ground belonging to a former leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of scrubby uncultivated land shares its name with Edward Heath, the 1970s British premier.

clue.text: His decimal system sounds a bit wet!

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: dewy means slightly moist, covered in dew

explanation.surface: A librarian's classification scheme is described as slightly damp.
explanation.walkthrough: Melvil Dewey devised the Dewey Decimal library classification.
explanation.definitionFit: Melvil Dewey's library classification is named after him, so the system is his.

clue.text: Song about daughter as woman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song's word goes round the letter for daughter

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A ballad about a daughter growing into a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous term for a female adult is a synonym for woman.

clue.text: Preminger going to and fro at the start

indicators.note: reads the same going either way, forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A film director going back and forth at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto Preminger was an Austrian-American film director; his first name reads the same in both directions, and 'at the start' hints that it is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The director Otto Preminger is known by that first name.

clue.text: Awful kids — crazy right through!

indicators.note: through means running inside, so the letter for right is placed within the word for crazy

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Badly behaved children are completely mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly, spoilt children are commonly called by this disparaging term.

clue.text: Two-wheeler destroyed by 100 lice

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A bike ruined by a hundred lice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered vehicle with two wheels.

clue.text: Shoes made of wood with square heel

annotationWithheld.why: Shoes made of wood with square heel (7): SANDAL from 'made of wood' is clear, but no reading of 'square heel' gives the final S
annotationWithheld.clue: Shoes made of wood with square heel

clue.text: The beginning of a book

definitions.meaning: the origin or creation of something
the first book of the Bible

explanation.surface: The opening chapter of some volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an origin, and it names the first book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Pops out through small doors?

definitions.meaning: small openings such as those in a deck or a serving wall

explanation.surface: Something emerges through little doorways.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicks emerge from eggs; small openings in decks or walls carry the same name.

clue.text: Wagon in which very ordinary passengers frolic

indicators.note: the wagon carries passengers, so the other letters ride inside it

parts.note: a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: Ordinary travellers having fun in a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap around excitedly, to play boisterously.

clue.text: Earthly inheritors with case of 17 appear quietly

parts.note: the Bible says the meek shall inherit the earth

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so take the first and last letters of the answer to 17

explanation.surface: Those who will inherit the earth appear with a woman's outer shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to 17-across, LADY, whose first and last letters give LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting humbly and submissively is acting without fuss or noise.

clue.text: Express irritation when pots are chucked back

indicators.note: chucked back means thrown in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pans are cooking pots

explanation.surface: Someone shows annoyance by throwing pots back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are chucked back' turns PANS to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap at someone is to speak sharply in annoyance.

clue.text: One's counterpart at work on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the work sits on top of the river

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: Someone's colleague working on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO is British slang for a colleague or opposite number.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a partner or opposite number.

clue.text: Place out an extraordinary melon variety

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Setting out an unusual type of melon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloupe is a type of musk melon with orange flesh.

clue.text: Bishopric a knight may try to get

parts.note: a see is the diocese of a bishop
K is the chess notation for king; here it is the abbreviation for knight as in KBE

explanation.surface: A knight attempts to win a bishop's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to go looking for something in order to obtain it.

clue.text: Stated rationale of former stance

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a stance is a position taken on an issue

explanation.surface: Someone's justification for a view they once held.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a detailed explanation setting out the reasoning behind something.
